disposition_mapping.rationale: Council consensus (pragmatist, finance_domain, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, and accounting_standards on reflection) is that due-item selection and proposal generation already happen as one system pass in modern ERPs and have no genuine judgment content once invoices are approved and matched. The merge is accepted on the condition emerging_economy and accounting_standards insisted on: the required input (approved matched invoices, PRE-R-01) survives explicitly, and the exception queue is sized to catch noisy/unreliable master data rather than assuming a clean input population — a human remains the accountable owner of exceptions, not a bystander to a fully autonomous pass.

Accounting_standards conceded in round 2 that the step boundary between selection and grouping carries no standards weight; what matters is that the merged step keeps currency-level visibility and keeps consuming approved matched invoices. PRE-R-08 (step must survive) is satisfied because proposal generation remains an identifiable function inside TGT-01, not because a human must press the button.

Decided against maximalist's flag-only/supervisor-on-exception design. The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) converged that vendor-bank-detail-change review is the highest-fraud-exposure control in the workflow and that a supervisor who only ever sees pre-filtered exceptions loses the pattern-sense needed to catch a convincing fake or a false negative the rules engine missed. Automation is retained for flagging only; the supervisor still reviews the full proposal and personally owns every hold/release decision, satisfying PRE-R-09, PRE-R-02 and PRE-R-03.

This was the sharpest council conflict: maximalist proposed an approval engine auto-clearing in-policy items with human involvement only on exception, against pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect and accounting_standards, all of whom held that delegated authority is a personal, accountable act that cannot be discharged by a policy-conformance check — and maximalist itself conceded this in round 2. Decision: every proposal receives an actual human approval act; automation (DOA validation/routing) may inform but never discharge it. This also protects KB-11's requirement that the derecognition-intent event have a determinable, independent anchor, and preserves PRE-R-04 and PRE-R-10.

Converged position (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect-after-concession, pragmatist-after-concession) over maximalist's single-agent straight-through design: automating file generation removes the incidental manual-build friction that today catches problems before transmission, so a deliberate replacement is required rather than silent deletion. The step is split into automated generation (TGT-04) and a dual-authorisation release gate (TGT-05) carrying a delta report and pre-transmission integrity check, with a named backup-releaser delegation chain to address emerging_economy's thin-headcount concern without collapsing the control's independence. PRE-R-05 and PRE-R-11 are satisfied across the pair.

Decided against folding confirmation receipt invisibly into posting (maximalist/agentic_architect's initial design). The majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer) held that this hides the queue of unmatched/delayed confirmations exactly when bank feeds are least reliable — precisely the condition under which it matters most. Kept as a distinct, visible, exception-owning step, tolerant of batch/manual reconciliation rather than assuming real-time API feeds, and required by accounting_standards to resolve confirmations to specific invoices/line items so KB-11's determinable-derecognition requirement is not lost in a merge.

Mechanical postings are automated, but three distinct exception classes are named explicitly per accounting_standards and agentic_architect's round-2 concessions: FX-variance beyond tolerance (KB-08), unmatched/partial settlement (KB-11), and period-cutoff breach (KB-03) — these are treated as separate failure dimensions, not substitutable by one tolerance rule. Emerging_economy's and accounting_standards' converged point on rate-source reliability (KB-02) is adopted as a standing human verification checkpoint for currency corridors subject to parallel-market distortion or thin published-rate coverage, going beyond a pure materiality-threshold model. PRE-R-06 and PRE-R-07 inputs are carried unchanged into TGT-07.

No KB principle bears directly on remittance mechanics (accounting_standards), and the baseline itself flags this as unconstrained_by_design. Full automation is adopted per broad council agreement, with two retained safeguards: multi-channel delivery (emerging_economy, since universal vendor email access cannot be assumed) and a named human-owned failed-delivery/dispute exception queue (hitl_designer, agentic_architect), so 'the system handled it' is never the final answer when the system is wrong.

steps.actor: AP automation agent, with AP analyst as exception-queue owner and run-parameter custodian
steps.description: An AP automation agent derives the due-item population from payment terms, approval status and currency flags, and groups items into a payment proposal by vendor, currency and payment method in the same system pass. Items that fail a selection rule (disputed holds, newly onboarded vendors, missing/ambiguous terms, FX items awaiting a rate decision) are routed to a visible, human-owned exception queue rather than silently included or dropped; the exception path is sized assuming master-data quality varies across entities, not just for rare edge cases. The AP analyst owns run parameters and the exception queue, not manual list curation.
steps.name: Automated due-item selection and proposal generation

steps.actor: AP supervisor, assisted by control-screening agent
steps.description: A control-screening agent pre-computes duplicate-payment, blocked-vendor and bank-detail-change flags against the payment history and change log, and ranks risk. The AP supervisor reviews the full proposal, not a flags-only summary, with visibility into what changed, when and by whom for every flagged item, and personally clears, holds or escalates each flagged item. Clean (unflagged) proposals are not auto-cleared by the same system that generated the flags; the supervisor's review and all dispositions are logged as structured, auditable decisions distinguishable from the agent's recommendation.
steps.name: AI-assisted proposal review

steps.actor: Authorised signatory, assisted by non-decisioning DOA validation/routing agent
steps.description: The authorised signatory personally approves every payment run; this is a human, accountable act on all items, not only exceptions. A delegation-of-authority validation agent checks amount/vendor/currency against delegated limits and pre-routes to the correct approver tier and presents the supervisor's flagged-item log for context, but it cannot approve or auto-clear items — it only validates and routes. Back-up/delegated approver chains are named system controls to cover leave, turnover or thin-headcount coverage without collapsing actor separation into a single person.
steps.name: Payment approval

steps.actor: Treasury automation agent, overseen by treasury officer
steps.description: A treasury automation agent converts the approved proposal into a bank payment file. An embedded, logged integrity check (hash/line-item match) verifies the generated file against the approved proposal before it can proceed to release, and a delta report is produced showing anything that changed since approval (late bank-detail amendments, value or batch-composition changes). File generation is mechanical and does not require a manual build, but it cannot itself transmit funds.
steps.name: Automated payment file generation

steps.actor: Second authorised releaser (treasury officer/manager, or system-enforced delegation chain, distinct from file-generation role)
steps.description: A second, independently credentialed releaser — distinct from whoever owns or configured the file-generation agent — authorises transmission, reviewing the integrity check and delta report as the control's defining artifact rather than a repeated summary of the approval. This is the irrevocable point of the workflow and retains a mandatory human gate even where generation is fully automated. Transmission supports a batch/store-and-forward fallback mode as a first-class operating mode, not only live API transmission, and a documented backup-releaser delegation chain exists for thin-staffed offices so the control does not collapse to one person wearing two hats.
steps.name: Dual-authorisation release to bank

steps.actor: Treasury officer, with automated matching engine
steps.description: Confirmations are auto-matched to the transmitted file at the individual invoice/line-item level (not aggregate bank totals), preserving the traceability needed to determine which specific payable was extinguished by which settlement. The mechanism tolerates delayed, end-of-day or manually downloaded statements as a normal operating mode, not only real-time webhook feeds. Unmatched, partial or rejected items are surfaced to a named human owner in a standing break queue rather than ageing silently or being absorbed invisibly into the posting step.
steps.name: Automated bank confirmation matching with break review

steps.actor: GL automation agent, with GL accountant owning exception review (FX variance, unmatched settlement, cutoff breach, rate-source verification for distorted-currency corridors)
steps.description: Mechanical settlement postings — clearing AP subledger open items and posting GL cash — are system-generated from the matched, invoice-level confirmation and the settlement-date rate. Exchange differences are posted as their own labelled line, never netted into cash. Three distinct exception classes route to the GL accountant: FX variances beyond tolerance, unmatched/partial settlements, and cutoff breaches near period-end, each requiring a period-gate check so settlement timing cannot drift postings into the wrong reporting period. Where the settlement currency is subject to parallel-market distortion, exchange controls or thin published-rate coverage, the rate source itself (not only the resulting variance) requires a standing human verification checkpoint for the affected corridors.
steps.name: Automated posting, clearing and FX-variance/cutoff review

steps.actor: AP analyst (automated generation/delivery, exception-queue owner for failed delivery)
steps.description: Remittance advice is generated and distributed automatically from the settlement confirmation, with per-invoice detail preserved. Multi-channel delivery (email, SMS, vendor portal, printed advice) is used rather than assuming universal reliable email access. Bounced or failed deliveries, and vendor remittance disputes, route to a named AP analyst exception queue rather than disappearing once the system has acted.
steps.name: Automated remittance advice distribution
